newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols spike on break below 114.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols spike on break below 114.

text.p: The retreat below 114 in spot dollar/yen early in the U.S. morning pushed one-month options implied volatility up sharply, traders said.
"Yen volatility is very spot-sensitive," said an East Coast U.S. bank dealer, noting foreign exchange market participants remained very concerned about downside risk in dollar/yen.
In this wary environment, dealers said, downdrafts in the dollar would continue to support volatility values.
"Both markets are very, very unstable. Anything goes," Masao Okada, chief dealer for Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York, said of spot and options trading.
Dollar/yen was at 113.50 and dollar/mark at 1.7315 in afternoon trading.
Last week, spot dollar/yen veered from a seven-month low near 110.60 on Wednesday back up to 115.80 the next day, catching many in the market off guard.

Traders are now trying to acquire as much volatility as possible to protect themselves in the event of another violent swing near-term, especially since dealers are short vega and gamma after selling options to satisfy the strong customer demand for yen calls in downside strikes, Okada said.

However, the upheaval of last week has left the market with a dearth of offers, forcing buyers to pay up this morning for at-the-money options and hiking up short-dated volatilities in the process, Okada said. "Nobody wants to trade aggressively," he observed.

One-month dollar/yen volatility jumped to 12.6/12.9 percent from 11.4/11.7 percent Friday, while one-year moved up only 0.05 point to 10.65/10.85 percent. One-month 25-delta risk reversals showed little change, retaining a yen call bias of 1.5/1.8.
Traders said one investor this morning was attempting to buy up to $500 million in low-delta 102 yen calls out two months.
One- to three-month yen calls in 107, 108 and 109 strikes were also popular.

Concern about protecting against more spot gyrations for the time being was taking precedence over trade data due out this week and the Group of Seven Denver summit this weekend, options dealers said. Japan's May trade report is scheduled for Tuesday and the U.S. April trade gap Thursday.

Dollar/mark volatility was calm by comparison as the spot held in a comfort zone between 1.7220 and 1.7420 marks after backing off from the upper end of the range on Friday, the U.S. bank dealer said.
"As long as we're in between those levels, there's really not much cooking," the bank dealer said.
Traders said that while many people expect the dollar to firm against European currencies over the intermediate term, the rise was expected to be slow and gradual.
The EU summit in Amsterdam today produced a compromise pact on European monetary union stability, reinforcing expectations for a soft single currency.
One-month dollar/mark volatility was 9.50/9.60 percent, up about 0.2 point from Friday, with one-year also little changed at 9.45/9.65 percent.
